after: ## How the HL extension fits the course
alt: The HL extension has three emphases: interconnection, complexity and tension, and solutions. Links to the common syllabus come from explicit mention in prescribed content, expanding a prescribed topic, or integrating thematic-study elements. It takes 80 of the 240 HL hours with no extra prescribed content.
caption: Spot connections, weigh tensions, then look for solutions.

alt: Eight topic areas arranged in a ring and all linked to each other: borders, environment, equality, health, identity, poverty, security and technology.
caption: Eight overlapping areas: the connections matter as much as the areas.

alt: Three groups of research questions for each case: background, data and issues; causes, impact and responses; and reflection. A case can be chosen topic-area first or case first. The minimum is two case studies across two topic areas.
caption: Three groups of questions turn a case into usable Paper 3 evidence.

alt: The 2016 to 2018 Cape Town drought mapped onto topic areas: environment, security and equality and poverty, where wealthier households could buy boreholes and tanks and poorer ones could not, plus the concepts legitimacy, power and interdependence. A Day Zero warning led to a 50-litre daily limit from February 2018; taps were never shut off.
caption: One case touches several topic areas; a second case adds comparison.

after: ## The six guiding lines of inquiry
alt: Six lines of inquiry: links to the core topics, links to the thematic studies, how far challenges are interconnected, how they are perceived and addressed in different contexts, which frameworks and mechanisms address them, and how cases from different areas change the view.
caption: Gather evidence for all six lines from every case.

after: ## Paper 3 exactly as the guide describes it
alt: Paper 3 lasts 90 minutes for 28 marks. Question 1 (3 marks, AO2) about 10 minutes; 2a (4 marks, AO2) about 13; 2b (6 marks, AO3) about 19; question 3 (15 marks, AO3) about 48 minutes. Question 3 is about 16% of the HL grade.
caption: Spend time where the marks are: question 3 deserves about half the paper.

after: ## Paper 3 exactly as the guide describes it
alt: A five-step frame for question 2b: action, actor, evidence, challenge and mitigation, illustrated with a heat-stoppage rule for the fictional Port Salem. Markbands: a vague recommendation scores 1 to 2; one that ignores difficulties 3 to 4; a well-supported one that considers challenges and consequences 5 to 6.
caption: Recommend, support, name the difficulty, then reduce it: that reaches the top band.
